title: RIPR Doctor Environment Report
description: The versioned JSON envelope emitted by `ripr doctor --json`. It reports the environment facts the human doctor screen prints: which checks ran, detected (not merely enabled) languages, unanalyzed source languages, preview-language enablement gaps, effective configuration defaults, seam-cache state, detected test surfaces, and the Perl preview/exporter state. These are static observations of one root and one host; none of them establish that analysis, verification, or a repair will succeed.

languages.description: Enabled language wire strings from the effective configuration. This is what `ripr.toml` turns on, NOT what the root contains; the marker scan's answer is `detected_languages`.

detected_languages.description: Languages the root marker scan found, whether or not the configuration enables them (schema 0.4). Omitted when no marker was found.

unanalyzed_source_languages.description: Source in languages no adapter reads, counted per language. A non-coverage disclosure, never a finding. Omitted when no such source exists.

preview_language_gaps.description: Detected preview languages `ripr check` skips until they are enabled. `config_entry` is what `[languages] enabled` accepts; `detected_language` is the source it analyzes, and the two differ for a JavaScript-only workspace (schema 0.4). Omitted when there is no such gap.

test_surfaces.description: The detected test surface per language. `framework` is null when no framework marker was confirmed; doctor never names a framework it did not read. Omitted when no language was detected.

doctor_status.description: The top-level outcome. `fail` is what maps to the exit code documented in docs/EXIT_CODES.md.

check_status.description: `skipped` marks a check that does not apply to this root and was not run; it never fails the report.

language_status.description: The capability tier `ripr check` treats the language as.

runtime_probe.description: One language runtime probe. `required` marks a probe whose failure fails the report; a language runtime is an analysis capability, not a prerequisite for building RIPR from source.

adapter_available.description: Whether the adapter was compiled into this binary. A detected language whose adapter is absent cannot be enabled at all.

enabled.description: Whether the effective configuration enables this language.

config_defaults.description: The effective configuration defaults. `null` when the configuration could not be loaded, so this field never claims a default the run did not verify. The `config` check owns that state and its evidence, which stays redacted per RIPR-SPEC-0007.

source_path.description: The `ripr.toml` this configuration was read from, or null when the built-in defaults apply.

cache_status.description: Where the seam cache lives for this root and how large it is. `size_bytes` is 0 when the directory does not exist or cannot be read, which is a legitimate state, not a failed measurement.

relocated_by_env.description: Whether RIPR_CACHE_DIR relocated the cache for this run.

binary_identity.description: The running binary and the `ripr` on PATH (schema 0.2). Advisory: its warnings never change `status` or the exit code.

perl_exporter_state.description: Compatibility is a capability probe, not an end-to-end proof: only `ripr check` validates an actual packet.

perl_preview.description: Perl preview state for a root whose marker scan found Perl. `null` when no Perl project was detected. Every field reports only what the static layer can determine; nothing here claims the producer works end to end (schema 0.4).

adapter_compiled.description: Whether this binary was built with the `lang-perl` Cargo feature.

ignored_configured_executable.description: A configured `[perl].executable` the opt-in gate refused to run. Reported so a user can see why the configured path was not probed.

frameworks.description: Perl test frameworks named by the `.t` sources. Empty means none were found.

runners.description: Perl test runners found on PATH. Empty means none were found.
